nodes.summary: A prefix of length `k ≤ card ι` has `k` elements.
nodes.title: Cardinality of a sorted prefix

nodes.summary: Categorical configuration priors are non-negative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of categorical configuration priors

nodes.summary: A normalized categorical prior, distinct from the cited coloc relative weights.
nodes.title: Normalized categorical colocalization prior

nodes.summary: A configuration Bayes factor is non-negative when both traits' Bayes factors are.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of configuration Bayes factors

nodes.summary: The Bayes factor of a configuration against the null: the product of the two traits' Bayes factors, `1` for a trait without a causal variant (the two studies are independent).
nodes.title: Bayes factor of a colocalization configuration

nodes.summary: Closed forms for the optional normalized categorical-prior model. This differs from the cited coloc formula only in using its remaining null mass rather than the cited H0 weight `1`.
nodes.title: Closed-form scores for the categorical colocalization prior

nodes.summary: The normalized posterior identity for the separate categorical-prior model.
nodes.title: Posterior identity for the categorical colocalization prior

nodes.summary: Cited coloc closed-form scores are non-negative on the Bayes-factor domain.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of closed-form colocalization scores

nodes.summary: The cited coloc closed-form algebraic scores. H0 has score `1`; H1--H4 retain the per-configuration coefficients of Giambartolomei et al. (2014). They are unnormalized hypothesis weights, and hence have a probability interpretation, when the Bayes factors are non-negative.
nodes.title: Closed-form colocalization hypothesis scores

nodes.summary: Cited coloc evidence is strictly positive for non-negative Bayes factors because H0 has unnormalized weight `1`.
nodes.title: Positivity of colocalization evidence

nodes.summary: The hypothesis of a configuration `(causal variant of trait 1, causal variant of trait 2)`, `none` meaning no causal variant.
nodes.title: Colocalization hypothesis of a causal configuration

nodes.summary: The five coloc hypotheses: no association (`h0`), trait 1 only (`h1`), trait 2 only (`h2`), two distinct causal variants (`h3`), one shared causal variant (`h4`).
nodes.title: The five colocalization hypotheses

nodes.summary: The unconditional algebraic coloc normalization identity: each hypothesis's configuration score divided by the total score equals its closed-form score divided by the closed-form total. For arbitrary real `bf1` and `bf2` these ratios need not be probabilities. See `colocPosterior_nonneg` and `sum_colocPosterior_eq_one` for the probability-domain results.
nodes.title: Colocalization normalization identity

nodes.summary: Normalized cited coloc hypothesis weights are non-negative for non-negative Bayes factors.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of colocalization posteriors

nodes.summary: Non-negative coloc configuration-weight parameters (Giambartolomei et al. 2014): `p1`, `p2`, `p12` for a variant causal for trait 1 only, trait 2 only, and both. The cited hypothesis weights use null weight `1`. The bound also supports a separate normalized categorical-prior model.
nodes.title: Colocalization prior parameters

nodes.summary: The effect posterior of the single-effect regression (Wang et al. 2020): given `y = x β + e` with `β ~ N(0, σ₀²)` independent of `e ~ N(0, σ² I)`, for almost every `y` the effect is normal with mean `σ₀² / (σ₀² + s²) · β̂` and variance `σ₀² s² / (σ₀² + s²)`, where `β̂ = olsEffect x y` and `s² = olsVar σ2 x`.
nodes.title: The effect posterior of the single-effect regression

nodes.summary: Strictly positive evidence has a strictly positive prior-weighted marginal likelihood.
nodes.title: Positivity of the prior-weighted marginal likelihood

nodes.summary: If the total mass is at least `ρ`, some prefix of length `k` is `ρ`-credible, has `k` elements, and every `ρ`-credible set has at least `k` elements.
nodes.title: A minimum-size credible set exists and is a sorted prefix

nodes.summary: A normalized non-negative finite prior assigns positive weight to some variant.
nodes.title: A normalized prior gives some variant positive weight

nodes.summary: The alternative marginal `N(0, V + W)` has density `wakefieldABF V W` with respect to the null law `N(0, V)`.
nodes.title: Wakefield's Bayes factor as a density ratio of Gaussians

nodes.summary: A `ρ`-credible set: its total posterior inclusion probability is at least `ρ`.
nodes.title: Credible set of variants

nodes.summary: The shortest credible prefix has minimum size (Maller et al. 2012; Wang et al. 2020): if `σ` sorts `α` in decreasing order and no prefix shorter than `k` is `ρ`-credible, every `ρ`-credible set has at least `k` elements.
nodes.title: The shortest credible prefix has minimum size

nodes.summary: If `y = x β + e` with `β ~ N(0, σ₀²)` independent of `e ~ N(0, σ² I)`, then `y` has density `multivariateGaussianPDFReal 0 (serCov σ2 σ02 x)`.
nodes.title: The marginal law of the phenotype given the causal variant

nodes.summary: The regression Bayes factor is the Wakefield ABF (Wang et al. 2020): the density of `y` when variant `x` carries an `N(0, σ₀²)` effect, divided by its density with no effect, is the ABF of the summary statistics `olsEffect x y` and `olsVar σ2 x`.
nodes.title: The regression Bayes factor is the Wakefield ABF

nodes.summary: Algebraic normalization of arbitrary weights times evidence. This is useful even outside the probability domain; it takes Lean's value `0` when the denominator vanishes.
nodes.title: Normalized weighted evidence

nodes.summary: The marginal least-squares effect estimate `xᵀ y / xᵀ x` of a variant with genotype vector `x`.
nodes.title: Marginal least-squares effect estimate

nodes.summary: The sampling variance `σ² / xᵀ x` of `olsEffect x y` for residual variance `σ²`.
nodes.title: Sampling variance of the least-squares effect estimate

nodes.summary: The remaining null mass in the optional normalized categorical-prior model.
nodes.title: Null mass of the categorical colocalization prior

nodes.summary: Posterior inclusion probabilities are non-negative when every evidence value is positive.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of posterior inclusion probabilities

nodes.summary: Posterior inclusion probability from a normalized non-negative prior and variant evidence. When every evidence value is positive, `PriorWeights.evidence_pos` makes the denominator strictly positive, and `pip_nonneg` and `sum_pip` prove that these values form a probability distribution.
nodes.title: Posterior inclusion probability

nodes.summary: `serCov σ2 σ02 x` is positive definite for `σ² > 0`.
nodes.title: Single-effect regression covariance is positive definite

nodes.summary: A finite probability distribution used as the prior over the single causal variant.
nodes.title: Prior weights over the causal variant

nodes.summary: If `β ~ N(0, W)` and the sampling error `ε ~ N(0, V)` are independent, the law of the estimate `β + ε` (alternative) has density `wakefieldABF V W` with respect to the law of `ε` (null).
nodes.title: The ABF is the Bayes factor

nodes.summary: The covariance `σ₀² x xᵀ + σ² I` of `y = x β + e` for `β ~ N(0, σ₀²)` and `e ~ N(0, σ² I)`.
nodes.title: Covariance of the single-effect regression model

nodes.summary: The unconditional algebraic single-effect likelihood-ratio identity for arbitrary real weights. Its right side is accurately named algebraic normalization, not a posterior probability.
nodes.title: Single-effect likelihood-ratio identity

nodes.summary: Posterior inclusion probabilities of the single-effect regression (Wang et al. 2020): Bayes' rule for the causal variant with a normalized non-negative prior equals `pip` applied to the strictly positive Wakefield ABFs.
nodes.title: Posterior inclusion probabilities of the single-effect regression

nodes.summary: The prior-weighted single-effect evidence is strictly positive on the regression domain.
nodes.title: Positivity of the single-effect regression evidence

nodes.summary: The first `k` variants in the order `σ`.
nodes.title: Prefix of variants in a given order

nodes.summary: The corresponding closed forms for the optional normalized categorical-prior model.
nodes.title: Categorical-prior hypothesis scores equal their closed forms

nodes.summary: The optional categorical configuration priors sum to one.
nodes.title: Categorical colocalization priors sum to one

nodes.summary: Normalized cited coloc hypothesis weights sum to one for non-negative Bayes factors.
nodes.title: Colocalization posteriors sum to one

nodes.summary: The coloc closed forms (Giambartolomei et al. 2014): the sum of unnormalized configuration weight times Bayes factor over each hypothesis equals its closed form.
nodes.title: The coloc closed forms

nodes.summary: The `k` largest values carry the most mass: if `σ` sorts `α` in decreasing order, no set of `S.card` variants has more mass than the prefix of that length.
nodes.title: Sorted prefix carries the most posterior mass

nodes.summary: Posterior inclusion probabilities normalize to one when every evidence value is positive.
nodes.title: Posterior inclusion probabilities sum to one

nodes.summary: With `z = b / √V`, `ABF = √(V / (V + W)) · exp (z² W / (2 (V + W)))`.
nodes.title: Wakefield's closed form

nodes.summary: Wakefield's ABF is strictly positive on its sampling-variance domain.
nodes.title: Positivity of Wakefield's approximate Bayes factor

nodes.summary: Wakefield's approximate Bayes factor: the `N(0, V + W)` density of the estimate `b` (its marginal law under the alternative `β ~ N(0, W)`) divided by its `N(0, V)` density (the null `β = 0`). Wakefield (2009) reports the reciprocal, null over alternative; coloc and SuSiE use this orientation, in which large values favor association. For `V = 0` the null density is Mathlib's junk value `0` and so is the ratio; the…
nodes.title: Wakefield's approximate Bayes factor

nodes.summary: Cited coloc configuration weights are non-negative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of colocalization configuration weights

nodes.summary: The cited coloc unnormalized configuration weight, whose H0 weight is `1`.
nodes.title: Unnormalized colocalization configuration weight
Probability

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
